08_interl2: to Jesus the Son of God
08_interl3: because "he came not to destroy the law, but to fulfil"
08_marg13: MOSES THE SERVANT. ADAMANTIUS. "Moses my servant is dead", etc. Mark how Jesus reigns. If you consider Jerusalem overthrown, the altar destroyed, nowhere any sacrifices or priests or pontiffs or any festivals of the Jews, you will say that Moses the servant of God is dead. If you consider the nations entering into the faith, churches built, altars not sprinkled with the gore of cattle but consecrated with the blood of Christ, priests and levites ministering not the blood of bulls or goats but the word of God through the grace of the Holy Ghost, you will say that after Moses Jesus holds the principality: not the son of Nave, but the Son of God; because Christ our Pasch is sacrificed, and we eat the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth. And there are the fruits of the good land in the Church, thirtyfold, sixtyfold, a hundredfold: the married, the widows, the virgins; and the seed of Israel is multiplied from those "who are born not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God"; and the children of God that were dispersed are gathered together in one. The people of God keeps sabbath not from common converse, but from every work of sin. Moses therefore, the servant of the Lord, is dead. Lastly, in a certain little book, although it is not held in the canon, the figure of this mystery is described. For it is related that two Moseses were seen, one living in the spirit and the other dead in the body. For the letter of the law, empty and void of all the things aforesaid, is Moses dead in the body; but the spiritual understanding of the law is Moses who lives in the spirit.
08_interl4: the law, which was as a pedagogue
08_interl5: according to the letter; but he lives in the spirit
08_interl6: of the living; "Blessed are the meek, for they shall possess the land"
08_marg14: "Now arise and pass over this Jordan", etc. See how Jesus the Son of God was the minister of Moses. "When the fulness of the time was come, God sent his Son, made of a woman, made under the law"; because he was made under the law of Moses, he was made the minister of Moses.
08_marg15: "Every place that you shall go up to with the soles of your feet I will give to you", etc. The letter of the law is laid on the ground and below. He therefore does not go up who follows the letter of the law. If you go up from the letter to the spirit, you go up to a high place, which you will receive from God as an inheritance. For if you understand that in the things that are written there are the forms of heavenly things, and seek the things that are above, where Christ is sitting at the right hand of God, then you will receive that place as an inheritance; because where Christ is, there also shall his minister be. If then you come by faith, life, virtue and purity even to Christ sitting at the right hand of God, and with those feet which Jesus Christ washed you walk upon that place, God will give it to you, that you may be made not only heir of God but joint heir with Christ.
08_interl11: "where I am, there also shall my minister be"
08_interl12: "The land that was desolate and impassable shall be glad", etc. And elsewhere: "Many are the children of the desolate, more than of her that hath a husband."
08_marg16: "The wilderness and before Libanus", etc. He did not say Libanus, but before Libanus, which Jesus receives from God; and "before Libanus" is said as it were for "in place of Libanus". If then you look at the former people, that is, Israel according to the flesh, which was the true olive, understand that it was the true Libanus. But because through its unbelief the kingdom is taken from it and given to a nation yielding the fruits thereof, this nation is before Libanus, that is, in the Church gathered from the Gentiles through Jesus Christ.
08_marg17: AS I HAVE BEEN WITH MOSES, SO WILL I BE WITH THEE, etc. AUGUSTINE. By this testimony and others Moses is proved to have died as the servant of God and pleasing to God, although in him that vengeance was fulfilled, that he did not enter into the land of promise; from which it is given to be understood that God takes some bodily or temporal vengeance on his good servants, and yet holds them among the vessels that are honourable and useful.
08_interl13: in prosperity, lest it soften thee; in adversity, lest it overthrow thee
08_marg18: AND JOSUE COMMANDED, etc. AUGUSTINE. It is asked how he commanded this after the Lord had exhorted him and strengthened him, promising that he would be with him, since it was many more days after that he crossed the Jordan. For when he had commanded these things, he sent spies into Jericho, who turned in to Rahab, and were hidden by her, and sought by the king and not found, she letting them down through the window and warning them to stay three days in the mountains. Four days therefore seem to have been spent in these things. And when they had reported what had been done concerning them, Jesus moved with all the people from the place where he was, early in the morning, and coming to the Jordan he turned aside. Then the people are admonished again to prepare themselves to cross the Jordan after three days. It was therefore a human arrangement that he first had it announced. For, as a man, he hoped this could be done if the spies returned quickly; and when they delayed, it is understood, even if Scripture is silent, that the rest was fulfilled by the disposition of God, that so Jesus might begin to be glorified among the people; whence it was said to him as he was about to cross the river: "This day I will begin to exalt thee before the children", etc. For even those with whom God is said to speak wish to do some things by human arrangement, in which they trust God to be their ruler; but their counsels are often changed by him by whose providence they are ruled. Whence Moses, as a man, thought that all the causes of the people were to be heard by him; [but] his arrangement was changed, Jethro suggesting it by divine inspiration.
08_marg19: ADAMANTIUS. Let us consider what figure the two tribes and a half hold, which receive their inheritance through Moses, and what the remaining nine and a half, which [receive] the promise of the holy land through Jesus. Those who receive their portion through Moses are all firstborn. For Ruben is the firstborn of Lia, Gad of Zelpha, Manasses of the daughter of the priest of Heliopolis, the wife of Joseph. In these, then, was already foreshadowed the figure of two peoples: one which should be firstborn by the order of nature, the other which should receive the inheritance through faith and the grace of the blessing. Nor is rest given first to those who receive the inheritance through Moses, that is, who pleased God through the law, unless they help their brethren in the battles. Yet the women and infants receive rest; the rest do not rest, but go out to the help of their brethren. When we strive in this life against the demons, there come to our help those who before the coming of Christ were justified in the law, as Isaias, Jeremias and the other prophets, by the reading of whom we are armed and enlightened. These are they who, as strong men armed and girded about the loins with truth, go out to our help and fight with us. But the infants and women do not go out to our battle. An infant is said to be one who does not speak. What then can he help me who has spoken nothing, whom I may read and whose word does not instruct me? The woman is the weaker vessel, nor does she come to the conflict, lest she be broken and perish; whence: the bruised reed he shall not break. Because, then, the women are commanded to be taught at home by their husbands, and signify those who learn rather than those who teach, they do not come to our help. For he can teach me nothing in whom I find nothing that I ought to imitate or hold.
08_interl14: the weaker vessels, not fit for the conflict, lest they be broken and perish; who are not permitted to teach, but only to be taught
08_interl15: who know not how to speak or teach
08_interl17: of the living, which they merited under the law
08_interl21: to the children of the New Testament
08_interl22: who were in the time of the Law
08_interl24: "I believe to see the good things of the Lord in the land of the living"
08_interl25: by instructing [you] how you should hold it
08_interl26: before the time of the New Testament
08_interl29: whence: "If you did believe Moses, you would believe me also"
08_marg20: Nor does it seem idle to me that the tribes which are dispensed through Moses are not three whole ones, nor those which obtain the inheritance through Jesus ten whole ones, but two and a half here and nine and a half there. But one is divided, by which neither the number three is filled up nor the number ten; because the former did indeed touch the knowledge of the Trinity, but not wholly nor perfectly, because they did not know the incarnation of the Only-begotten. For although they believed in his coming and his other dispensations, and even preached them, yet they could not see and behold what they had believed; whence: many prophets and kings have desired to see the things that you see, etc. For their faith was not whole, because the dispensation of the flesh had not yet been fulfilled, and what we believe already done they believed would be done. Those tribes, then, are neither two, lest the fathers be outside the faith and salvation of the Trinity, nor three whole and perfect, lest the sacrament of the Trinity should seem fulfilled in them. But they did touch the third number, because they desired to see whom we see, and could not. Perhaps not even at the coming of Jesus do we learn what is perfect and whole, nor if he be led to the cross and consummated in all things, nor if he rose from the dead; [the Spirit] will show us through himself all things that are perfect. Whence: "I have yet many things to say to you, but you cannot bear them now"; "But when the Spirit of truth is come, who proceedeth from the Father", etc. You see that not only with Moses is the number three imperfect, but Jesus still says to his disciples: You cannot hear them now. He hints at the Spirit of truth, because through the Holy [Spirit] and in him the perfection of the Trinity is fulfilled.
08_marg21: There are nine and a half tribes which are governed under Jesus, not ten whole ones, which is a perfect number; so that what is said to be reserved by the Lord Jesus for the Holy Ghost may seem half full and in the middle. For although through Christ penance is preached, and conversion, and remission of sins is given, and all the things that seem to tend to the perfection of the number ten, yet the perfection and sum of all goods is if, after all these things, one merits to receive the grace of the Holy Ghost.
08_marg22: Moreover, in this book it is written that the true altar was in that land which Jesus distributed. But Ruben and Gad and the half tribe of Manasses made for themselves an altar not true, but one that should bear the type of the true altar, which was with Jesus. What wonder, then, if they did not receive the whole knowledge of the Trinity, who had built neither a whole nor a true altar? Therefore neither many enemies nor more kings of the hostile powers were cast down by them. Only Sehon king of the Amorrhites, and Og king of Basan, and the Amalecites did they cast down beyond the Jordan. But where Jesus led the army, now five kings fall together, who had fled into caves, and are hanged on a tree; now thirty are slain together; and they exterminate all who possess the holy land with uncleanness, who hold the land flowing with milk and honey in the bitterness of malice.
08_interl32: the two testaments, that he might prove the faith of believers or the unbelief of the rebellious before the coming of the judgment
08_interl34: namely, of the Church gathered from the Gentiles, which before committed fornication with idols in the desires of the flesh; whence: "The harlots shall go before you into the kingdom" of heaven
08_marg23: ADAMANTIUS. Spies are sent by Jesus into Jericho and are received by the harlot Rahab. These spies may be thought to be angels, according to that: "Behold I send my angel before thy face", etc.; which was fulfilled through others invisibly, but through John visibly, of whose baptism it is said that the scribes and Pharisees did not believe him; but the harlots and publicans, believing, were baptized; as the harlot received the spies of Josue, through whom she is rescued from the destruction of the hostile nation. Rahab is interpreted breadth. This is the Church of Christ, which, gathered from sinners as from harlotry, says: "The place is too strait for me, make me room to dwell in"; "and who hath brought up these for me?"; and to whom it is said: Enlarge thy dwellings. This is the harlot to whom Solomon, who came to make peace between the things that are in heaven and the things that are on earth, commanded the living child to be given back. But she who had the dead child is the synagogue of the former people, or of those who have turned aside into heresy. This harlot receives the spies of Jesus, and having received them sets them in the upper places, namely, in the high sacraments of the faith. For no one sent by Jesus is found below and lying on the ground, but he remains in the upper places. Nor does he alone remain in the upper places, but the harlot also who receives him from a harlot becomes a prophetess. For she says: "I know that the Lord hath given you this land", etc. You see how she who was once an impious and unclean harlot is now filled with the Holy Ghost: she confesses the past, believes the present, prophesies the future. So Rahab is enlarged and advances until their sound went forth into all the earth. Japheth also is interpreted enlargement, who himself bore the figure of the Gentile people; and Chanaan the boy is made subject to him as a servant by his father, and to his brother Sem, in the figure of those who are saved from the circumcision. In which is the wonderful kindness and providence of God, who, wishing to bestow remedy and salvation on the sinner Cham, made him the servant of his brethren, as Esau of his brother Jacob: not that he might perish, but that by obeying his betters he might gain salvation. For very much is bestowed on the wicked who know not how to rule themselves when they are not entrusted to themselves but become the servants of the saints and are subject to their betters. You see how great the kindness of the Lord, which he hides from the ears of the crowd and covers with harsher words, lest the bad and ungrateful servant become a despiser if he understand the goodness in the mercy of his Lord.
08_interl35: to the devil, or the world, which would rather be in danger than lose the spies of Christ
08_interl39: she makes a covenant for her own safety and that of her household with the testaments of the Lord
08_interl40: from the ruin of the world
08_interl41: as if [to say]: flee lowly and abject things, preach heavenly things
08_marg24: GET YE UP TO THE MOUNTAINS. ADAMANTIUS, etc. The wise harlot gives mystical and heavenly counsel, having nothing earthly. Go away, she says, by the mountains; do not walk through the valleys; flee lowly and abject things; preach the things that are lofty and sublime. And she herself puts a scarlet cloth in her house, through which she may be saved from the destruction of the city: scarlet, namely, because it bore the figure of blood. For she knew that there was salvation for none except in the blood of Christ. This commandment also is given her: All who shall be found in thy house shall be saved. If then any one wishes to be saved, let him come into this house in which the blood of Christ is in sign of redemption. For with those who said, "His blood be upon us and upon our children", the blood of Christ is unto damnation. For Jesus is set for the fall and for the resurrection of many. Therefore to those who gainsay his sign the blood becomes unto punishment, to believers unto salvation. No one therefore is saved outside the Church. He who goes out becomes guilty of his own death; this is the sign of blood, because this is the sanctification that consists through blood. That this sign hangs in the window I think indicates this: the window lights the house, and through it we take in as much light as suffices for our eyes and sight; and the incarnation of the Saviour did not bring before us the whole sight of the Godhead, but as through a window, through his incarnation he made us behold the light of the Godhead. Therefore it seems to me the sign of salvation was given through the window, by which all who are in her house, she who was once a harlot, obtain salvation, cleansed in water and in the Holy Ghost and in the blood of Christ.
08_interl46: no one is saved outside the Church
08_marg25: WHEN YOU SHALL SEE. AUGUSTINE. The scribes say to the people: "When you shall see the ark of the testimony of our God, and the priests and the levites carrying it, set out from your places and go after it. But let there be a long space between you and it, as much as two thousand cubits; you shall stand, lest you come near it, that you may know the way by which you shall go in it; for you have not gone the way yesterday and the day before", etc. The ark was commanded to go far ahead, so that it could be seen by the people; for so great a host, if it went close behind it, would not see it going before, nor know where to follow. From this it is understood that the pillar of cloud, which used to give the signal for moving camp and to show the way, had already withdrawn and no longer appeared to them. Hence it came about that those three days were foretold by human arrangement. Now therefore, under the leadership of Jesus, they follow the ark of the Lord, the cloud being withdrawn as though a veil were taken away.
08_interl47: Christ is exalted for each one when he is baptized in his death
08_marg26: ADAMANTIUS. Many wonders were done in the wilderness, and nowhere is Jesus said to be exalted. But where the Jordan is crossed it is said to him: "This day I will begin to exalt thee", etc. For the exaltation of Jesus in the sight of the people takes its beginning from baptism. For those who are baptized are baptized in his death, whose death is completed in the exaltation of the cross. Rightly, then, for each of the faithful Jesus is first exalted when he comes to the mystery of baptism; whence: God hath exalted him, and hath given him a name, namely, which is above every name, etc.
08_marg27: ADAMANTIUS. To the sinner every creature is an enemy, as to the Egyptians the river, the earth, the sky. To the just all things serve. He crosses the Red Sea with dry foot; the Egyptian is drowned. In the wilderness, that is, in the desert, horrible and vast, food is ministered from heaven to the just; and in the Jordan the ark of the testament is leader to the people; the waters failed before the priests and levites. Likewise to thee, who through the sacrament of baptism hast come forth from the streams of the Jordan, a passage through the very air is promised; whence: "We shall be taken up to meet Christ, into the air", etc. There is nothing then for the just to fear, whom every creature serves, and to whom it is said: "When thou shalt pass through the fire, the flame shall not burn thee", etc. And all the things that were done among the former are fulfilled in thee according to the mystical sense, who desirest, leaving the darkness of idolatry, to come to the hearing of the divine law. Thou leavest Egypt. When thou art gathered with the catechumens and hast begun to obey the precepts of the Church, thou hast also gone out through the Red Sea, and, set in the stations of the desert, thou givest thyself daily to hearing the law of God and beholding the face of Moses revealed through the glory of the Lord. But if thou come to baptism and, the order of priests and levites standing by, art initiated into the venerable sacraments, then by the ministry of the priests thou shalt cross the Jordan and enter the land of promise; in which, after Moses, Jesus receives thee, the leader of the new journey. And thou, mindful of such great powers, that the sea was divided for thee, that the water of the Jordan stood, wilt say: "What ailed thee, O thou sea, that thou didst flee: and thou, O Jordan, that thou wast turned back?" And the divine word will answer: "At the presence of the Lord the earth was moved, at the presence of the God", etc.
08_marg28: Chanaanite: possessing, or possession, or merchants, or changeable. Hethite: fearing, or astonished. Hevite: gathering stones. Pherezite: separating, or sowing abroad. Gergesite: bringing near a husbandman, or casting out a husbandman, or a stranger drawing near. Amorrhite: bitter, or speaking. Jebusite: treading, or their manger.
08_interl48: because through the teaching office of the priests the people is led to the land of promise; and if anyone today is worthy to be enrolled in that order, the very streams of the Jordan will yield to him and the very elements will reverence him
08_interl49: because [they are] a part of those who are baptized; they keep the sweetness of heavenly grace received
08_marg29: The Seventy: "As in the days of wheat harvest." This seems incredible in our regions. But there, as those who know it relate, at the beginning of spring is the wheat harvest; and then that river overflows and is filled more than in winter.
08_interl50: because a part is turned into the bitterness of sins
08_marg30: ADAMANTIUS. I think it is not written without a mystical reason that part of the waters of the Jordan is sunk into the sea and flows into bitterness, while part remains in sweetness. For if all who are baptized kept the sweetness of heavenly grace, none would be turned into the bitterness of sins. But often, having received baptism, they return to worldly things and drink the salt cup of avarice, and flowing into the sea they perish in the salt waves. But that part which remains in stability and keeps its sweetness signifies those who hold firmly the gift of God received. And rightly is the part of those who are saved one, because one is the bread that came down from heaven, and one faith, and one baptism, and one Spirit with which all are given to drink in baptism, and one God the Father of all.
08_interl52: who teach the people to go out of Egypt, that is, out of the errors of the world, and to pass through the wilderness, that is, the temptation of the world
08_marg31: THE PRIESTS that, etc. The same priestly and levitical order stands by the ark of the Lord, in which the law of God is carried. For they are those who enlighten the people from the commandments of God. Whence: "Thy word is a lamp to my feet, and a light to my paths"; this light is kindled through the priests and levites.
08_marg32: THE PEOPLE, he says, is to be far from the ark of the testament of the Lord, two thousand cubits; but the priests and levites near, that it may be carried on their shoulders. Blessed are they who merit to be near to God. But it is written: "They who draw near to me draw near to fire." If thou be gold and silver and draw near to the fire, thou wilt shine the brighter through the fire. If thou hast built upon [the foundation] wood, hay, stubble, thou wilt be consumed. Blessed then are they who are near, so that the fire enlightens them and does not burn them. Israel shall indeed be saved, but, set far off, it makes its journey not by its own power, [but] in the ministry of the priests.
08_marg33: AUGUSTINE. How for ever, when heaven and earth pass away? Is it because they signify something eternal, though they themselves cannot be eternal? Although what is in the Greek could be said in Latin "unto the age".
08_interl53: we are not to act idly or slackly, but all the precepts of the Lord are to be passed through and fulfilled with haste
08_marg34: ADAMANTIUS. Those who crossed the Red Sea were baptized in Moses, in the cloud and in the sea; and of those who cross the Jordan we can likewise say that all were baptized in Jesus in the Jordan. What is written, "and the people made haste and passed over the Jordan", I do not think is idle. For when we come to baptism and receive the sacrament of the word of God, we must not act sluggishly but make haste until we pass through all things, that is, fulfil all the commandments, that we may merit to come to the promised beatitude. But when we have passed through all things, we must walk diligently and warily, lest our steps be suddenly poured out; whence: My steps had well nigh slipped. Nor ought care to be slacker in keeping the virtues than in acquiring them; which is designated when it is said that forty thousand men girded in truth crossed over to take Jericho: girded, namely, with the girdle of truth; whence: "Stand therefore, having your loins girt about with truth." Our girdle too ought to be of truth, if indeed we keep the sacrament of this warfare and girdle; if we speak falsehood, we are ungirt of the belt of truth. Let us then be girded in truth, but ungirt in falsehood. Crossing the Jordan, we cross to wars against the spirits of wickedness in high places. For all these things were written for us. Let us go out then to war, that the first city of this [world], namely the malice of the world and its proud walls, may be taken by us. Within thee is the battle; within thee is the evil building to be overthrown; thy enemy proceeds from thy heart. "For from the heart come forth evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, fornications", etc. You see how great and of what kind is the army of thy enemies. These must be overthrown by us in the first slaughter, that we leave none. Then through Jesus that rest will be given us, that "every one shall rest under his vine and under his fig tree, since there is none now to make the children of Israel afraid".
08_interl54: as teachers and leaders to the land of promise
08_interl55: because, when we have passed through all things, we must go diligently and warily, lest our steps be poured out
08_interl56: broad and spacious is the way of Jericho, that is, of the world
08_interl57: the malice of the world and the proud walls of sin are first to be overthrown by us
08_interl58: he who is under the law fears Moses; when one passes to the Gospel, the observance being changed, the fear is changed; whence: "I through the law am dead to the law, that I may live to God", etc.
08_marg35: Jesus was always exalted with the Father, but there is need that God exalt him in our sight, that is, that we know the height of his divinity. And this is done if we cross the Jordan and are armed for the wars to come with the various defences of the sacraments.
08_marg36: AUGUSTINE. "Command the priests that carry the ark of the testament", etc. It is usually said the ark of the testament or the ark of the testimony. Now therefore it is said the ark of the testament of the testimony, so that not only the ark but the testament itself is called the testament of the testimony. For hence the Apostle says: "But now without the law the justice of God is made manifest, being witnessed by the law and the prophets"; because the Old Testament was given in testimony of the thing to come.
08_marg37: That is, the day on which the mystery of the lamb was commanded in Egypt; because on the same day that we flee the errors of the world we enter the land of promise. For the whole present life is one day; today, then, that is, while we live, let us hasten to perfection, and not put it off till tomorrow.
08_marg38: ADAMANTIUS. Not without cause is it marked when they come to the Jordan: on the tenth, he says, of the first month. This is the very day on which the mystery of the lamb was commanded in Egypt; on the same they enter the land of promise. And it is very blessed that on the very day on which one escapes the errors of the world he should enter the land of promise, that is, on this day on which we live in this world; for the whole present life is signified by one day. By this, then, we are taught not to put off the works of justice till tomorrow, but today, that is, while we live, to hasten to fulfil all the things that pertain to perfection. And so we shall be able on the tenth day of the first month to enter the land of promise, that is, the beatitude of perfection. And note that this day is often repeated, because, although there is for us one general perfection, yet if we can fulfil wholly one kind of virtue, that very virtue has each its own perfection. Thus through the several virtues many perfections are found. But that is the general one which contains in itself the sum of all perfections. Therefore on this day many deeds are recapitulated, to signify that many perfections pertain to one day.
08_marg39: ISIDORE. The children of Israel, crossing the Jordan, took from the midst of the river twelve stones, which they set up for a testimony in the place of the second circumcision, to signify to us that when we rise from the laver we ought to carry with us the most firm examples of the apostolic life, whose testimony we should ever look upon for the imitation of the virtues.
08_interl59: because in the rock, which is Christ, we are cleansed and lay aside the reproach of Egypt, that is, the observances of the Egyptians
08_marg40: AUGUSTINE. "Make thee knives of sharp stone, and sitting circumcise the children of Israel again." It is asked why he said "again". For not one man was to be circumcised twice; but because one people was in some circumcised, in some not circumcised, therefore it is said "again", that the circumcised might be circumcised again: not the man but the people. Some sons of those who went out of Egypt were uncircumcised in that people, whom Jesus could circumcise: their sons, namely, whom they begot in the desert and scorned to circumcise, because they were disobedient to the law of God. Why then do they think that those who have the sacrament of Christian baptism are to be rebaptized, as though helped by this testimony of the law? Since not one man was circumcised twice, but the people, which had been circumcised in some and uncircumcised in others; even if in some way it could happen that God commanded a man to be circumcised twice, can those who think men are to be rebaptized say that it was commanded because they had been circumcised by Egyptians, or by some heretics separated from the fellowship of the Israelites?
08_marg41: MAKE THEE KNIVES OF STONE, and sitting circumcise the children of Israel. Let the Jews say how one can be circumcised a second time with carnal circumcision. For one once circumcised has nothing that can be taken away a second time. But by us, to whom it is said that the law is spiritual, these things are fitly and suitably solved. For he who has been instructed in the law through Moses has laid aside the error and worship of idolatry. This is the first circumcision, through the law. But if he come to the Gospel, he will receive the second circumcision through the rock, which is Christ, and the reproach of Egypt will be taken away from him. For unless one has been cleansed by the second circumcision through the Gospel, he does not lay aside the reproach of Egypt. For even if all come from the law and are instructed through Moses, they yet have the reproach of sins; whence Paul also: "For we ourselves also were some time unwise, incredulous, erring, slaves to divers desires and pleasures", etc. But after Christ came, and through baptism circumcised a second time and cleansed our souls, we cast away all these things, and in their place took up the answer of a good conscience toward God. Let no one, then, if he has been wholly converted and has repented from the heart, faithfully crossed the Jordan and received the second circumcision, fear the reproaches of past sins, hearing: "This day I have taken away from thee the reproach of Egypt"; whence elsewhere: "Thy sins are forgiven thee"; "but now sin no more, lest some worse thing happen to thee". For if after the remission of sins thou sin no more, truly the reproach of Egypt is taken away from thee. But if thou sin again, the reproaches of Egypt will roll back upon thee again, and the more so because it is of greater crime to tread under foot the Son of God and esteem the blood of the testament unclean than to neglect the law of Moses. For he who commits fornication under the Gospel is of far greater reproach than he who does so under the law, because, taking the members of Christ, he makes them the members of a harlot. In short, no one charges him with lewdness, but condemns him for the crime of sacrilege, because it is said to him: "Know you not that your bodies are the temple of God?" If any man violate the temple of God, him shall God destroy. Moreover, he that committeth fornication sinneth against his own body: not only this body, which by hearing the word of God and retaining it in the heart has been made the temple of God, but also that of which it is said that the whole church is the body of Christ; and he who has stained his own body seems to sin against the whole church, because through one member the stain spreads into the whole body.
08_interl60: the people, namely, not one man
08_marg42: ADAMANTIUS. Those who had not been obedient to the commandments of the Lord are called uncircumcised; from which it is understood that those are called uncircumcised who do not obey the commandments of God. But because God loves every soul, he sent Jesus the Son of God to circumcise both the worthy and the unworthy: not the son of Nave, who did not truly and perfectly circumcise the people, but Jesus the Son of God, who truly cleansed body and soul from every defilement of sin.
08_interl61: whose fathers, disobedient to the law, disdained to circumcise them
08_interl63: that is, until they did with love what before seemed difficult
08_marg43: "And the children of Israel, being circumcised, rested in the same place, sitting in the camp until they were healed." It is not enough to be circumcised. After circumcision there is need to be healed and for a scar to form over the wound. To be circumcised through Jesus, then, is to lay aside vices and depraved habits and the worst ways, and to cut off whatever is at variance with the rule of honesty. But in doing this we are constrained by a certain difficulty, and with a certain pain of mind we avoid the fault of habit by a new way of life. In this time, then, we are said to remain as it were in the pain of our circumcision until the scar forms and we are healed, that is, until we fulfil the new ways without difficulty and what before seemed unaccustomed and difficult turns into habit; and then it will rightly be said to us: "This day have I taken away the reproach of Egypt from you."
08_interl64: all the vices and sins of the Egyptians
08_interl65: that is, revelation; because while one walks in the foreskin of unbelief through the desert of this life he is blind; but as soon as he is circumcised his eyes are opened
08_interl66: after the second circumcision and the healing
08_marg44: After the reproach of Egypt was taken away, the children of Israel kept the Pasch on the fourteenth day of the month. For neither before circumcision, nor after it before they were healed, could they eat the flesh of the lamb. You see then that no unclean man keeps the Pasch, no uncircumcised man; whence: "Christ our pasch is sacrificed; therefore let us keep the feast, not with the old leaven, nor with the leaven of malice and wickedness, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth."
08_marg45: ISIDORE. After the circumcision of the Gospel, at once in the place of revelation the Pasch is celebrated and the lamb is sacrificed that taketh away the sins of the world; and, the manna of the figurative law failing, the people first eats the bread of the body of Christ, which the incorrupt land of promise, that is, the Virgin Mary, brought forth, whose grain, falling into the earth, brought forth much fruit. Note the order: after, with Jesus Christ as leader, we pass through the streams of the laver, and are signed by faith with the spiritual circumcision, then at last we celebrate the Pasch, that is, we believe that Christ was sacrificed for the salvation of the world, and, believing, we are at once fed with the bread of the Lord's [body].
08_marg46: ADAMANTIUS. When the people went out of the land of Egypt, they carried dough with leaven in their garments. When this had failed, manna was given them. But when they came to the holy land and took the fruits of the province of palms, the manna failed them, and they began to eat of the fruits of the land. Three kinds of food, then, are described in general: one on which we feed when going out of the land of Egypt, but this suffices for a short time; after this the manna succeeds; the third we take from the holy land. The fruit that we carry with us from Egypt is this small schooling, or perhaps that of the liberal letters, which can help somewhat. In the wilderness, that is, in the state of this life, we feed on manna while we are instructed in the learning of the divine law. But those who have merited to enter the land of promise, that is, to obtain the promises of Christ, will eat fruit from the region of palms. For he truly will find the fruit of the palm who, the enemy being conquered, shall come to the promises. For however much we may understand in the divine letters, far more sublime will be the things which we shall see not in a riddle but face to face; because eye hath not seen, nor [ear heard], what things God hath prepared … But if the law is taken according to the letter, the children of Israel are found, when they were using better things (for they received manna from heaven by promise), to have received worse; they to whom, when the foods of Egypt failed, a better food, that is, manna, had succeeded. For how is it thought that, the better food ceasing, a worse succeeded?
08_interl67: because "when that which is perfect is come, that which is in part shall be done away"
08_interl69: AUGUSTINE. The Seventy: "In Jericho": not in the city itself, namely, which was not yet taken, but in the field belonging to it
08_interl70: we first lift up our eyes when we begin to see Christ
08_interl71: the ready sentence by which Jericho was to be punished
08_marg47: ADAMANTIUS. "It came to pass, when Jesus was in Jericho, looking up with his eyes he saw a man standing over against him, and a drawn sword was in his hand; and Jesus going to him said to him: Art thou ours, or of the adversaries?" Looking up with his eyes he saw the prince of the host of the power of God, as though he had not looked before; but then, when he was to see the prince of the host of the Lord, he did not see him as a common man, but understood him to be a certain power. He is not yet certain whether what is seen is a divine power or an opposing one; therefore he says: "Art thou ours, or of the adversaries?" "And he said: I am the prince of the host of the power of the Lord; now I am come." When Jesus heard this he adored and said: "Lord, what dost thou command thy servant?" Jesus teaches the same as the Apostle: "Believe not every spirit, but try the spirits if they be of God." Jesus therefore knew not only that he was of God, but that he was God. For he would not have adored unless he had known God. For who else is the prince of the host of the powers but Christ? For the whole host of heaven, whether angels or archangels or virtues or dominations, ever [fights]; all things were made through him, and they serve under him as prince, who is the prince of princes and bestows principality on princes; who says: "Have thou power over ten cities", etc.; who, having received the kingdom, returned.
08_interl72: to cut away the filth of our flesh
08_interl73: believe not every spirit; hence it is said to Jeremias: "If thou wilt separate the precious from the vile, thou shalt be as my mouth"
08_interl74: Christ is the prince of the heavenly host, because "all things were made by him" and he gave to each his principality
08_marg48: It can be asked whether he prostrated himself to an angel and called him Lord, or rather, because he understood that it was God, understanding by whom he had been sent, he called him Lord and prostrated himself to him.
08_interl75: because he understood that it was God
08_marg49: ISIDORE. Jesus is in Jericho. The enemies still hold the city, not yet taken; and yet it is said to Jesus: "Loose, saith he, thy shoe; for the place in which thou standest is holy ground." How is Jericho holy ground, which is held by the enemies? But perhaps wherever the prince of the power of the Lord comes, he sanctifies the place. I dare further and say: where Moses stood, the place was not of itself holy, but the presence of the Lord who was with him had sanctified the place; therefore it is said to him: "The place in which thou standest is holy ground", etc. And we, if by life and merits we draw near to God and are made worthy that God should stand by us, will be told to loose from the feet of our soul whatever mortal bond is in them. For these are the feet which Jesus washed, and unless he wash them we shall have no part with him. If then we loose from our soul and senses every bond of mortal guilt, at once God gladly cleaves to us and stands by us.
08_interl77: namely, of the soul, which unless Jesus wash we shall have no part with him
08_marg50: THE SAME. Jericho is surrounded, and it must be taken. No sword is drawn against it, no bow or ram is aimed at it, nor are darts hurled; only trumpets are applied by the priests, and by them the walls of Jericho are overthrown. Jericho signifies this world. Whence: a certain man went down from Jerusalem to Jericho and fell among robbers: he was the figure of Adam, who was thrust out of paradise into the exile of this world. The blind also who were in Jericho, whom God enlightened, signified those who in this world were oppressed by the blindness of ignorance. Jericho, then, that is, the world, is to fall. For the consummation of the world has long since been published in the holy volumes; and the consummation will come about by the voices of trumpets; whence the Apostle: "For the trumpet shall sound, and the dead" who are in Christ [shall rise] first; and the Lord himself shall come down from heaven with commandment, and with the voice of an archangel, and with the trumpet of God. Then therefore Jesus will conquer Jericho with trumpets and lay it low, so that out of it the harlot alone is saved and all her house. Jesus therefore will come, and with the voice of trumpets. But even now let us pray that he come and destroy that world which is seated in wickedness, and all the things that are set in the world; because all that is in the world is the concupiscence of the flesh, and the concupiscence of the eyes, and the pride of life. But let him save this one alone, who received his spies, who set his apostles, received in faith and obedience, in the upper places; and let him join this harlot with the house of Israel. But let us no longer reckon her old fault: once she was a harlot; but now she is joined as a chaste virgin to one husband, Christ. Whence: "I have espoused you to one husband, that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ." For, that she might escape and not perish with Jericho, she received from the spies a most powerful sign of salvation, the scarlet cord; for through the blood of Christ the Church is saved.
08_marg51: JERICHO is interpreted moon. And the moon signifies the world, because, as the moon wanes in its monthly courses, so this world, running toward the consummation of the times, falls by daily waning. In the ark the Church is figured; the strong preachers in the trumpets of brass. For the Israelites, bearing the ark, go round this city of Jericho for seven days with brazen trumpets sounding, and its walls fall at the presence of the ark and the sound of the trumpets. For in this time, which revolves in the succession of seven days, while the ark is carried, that is, while the Church, going round the whole world, is moved, at the voices of the preachers, as at the sound of the trumpets, the walls of Jericho, that is, the obstacles of the world's pride and of the haughtiness of unbelief, fall; until at the end of the times the last enemy, death, is destroyed, and from the perdition of the wicked the one house of Rahab, that is, the Church, is freed, cleansed from the filthiness of fornication, through the window of confession, in the blood of remission. For this harlot dwells in Jericho, that is, in this mortal body, that is, in the world; who, that she may be saved, puts out the scarlet through the window of her house, as through the mouth of her body, which is the sign of the blood of Christ, confessing unto salvation through the remission of sins. Those who were found in her house were saved from the destruction of the city; and whoever are found within the Church are saved. Outside this house, that is, outside the Church, no one is saved.
08_interl80: by worldly cunning, or blocked up
08_interl86: the demons, or any who are mighty in the world
08_interl88: through the whole time of the present life
08_interl89: for the consummation of the world has long since been published in the holy volumes
08_interl90: which now sounds, now is silent
08_marg52: ADAMANTIUS. Jericho is overthrown by the trumpets of the priests: for as soon as the blare of the trumpets sounded, the walls were cast down. For we see that the strength of the world and its defences have been destroyed by the priestly trumpets: namely, the worship of idols, the deceit of divinations supplied by the art of demons, the contrivances of augurs, soothsayers and magicians, by all which, as by walls, the world was surrounded. Besides, it was fortified as by tall and strong towers by the various doctrines of the philosophers, their most lofty assertions and disputations. But Jesus Christ, coming, sent priests, that is, his apostles, bearing the beaten trumpets of preaching, the holy, magnificent and heavenly doctrine. Matthew first sounded the priestly trumpet in his Gospel. Mark also and Luke and John sang with these trumpets. Peter resounds with the two trumpets of his epistles; James also and Jude and John sound the trumpet through their epistles, and Luke describing the acts of the apostles. Last, Paul, thundering forth fourteen epistles, overthrew as with trumpets the walls of Jericho, and all the engines of idolatry and the doctrines of the philosophers.
08_interl91: because at the consummation of the world the trumpet shall sound, and the dead who are in Christ shall rise first, and the Lord himself shall come down from heaven with the trumpet of God
08_marg53: ADAMANTIUS. "Keep yourselves from the anathema, lest perhaps you covet and take of the anathema, and make the camp of the children of Israel an anathema, and crush yourselves and all the synagogue of the Lord." As if [to say]: see that you have nothing worldly in you, nor bring anything of the world with you to the Church, but let all worldly conversation be an anathema to you. Do not mingle worldly things with divine; as if [to say]: "Love not the world, nor the things which are in the world"; whence: "Be not conformed to this world", etc. For those who do these things take of the anathema. Those Christians also who celebrate the solemnities of the Gentiles bring the anathema into the Church; and those who inquire into the lives and deeds of men from the courses of the stars, and those who observe the flight of birds and the like, pollute the camp of the Lord and cause the people of God to be conquered. For a little leaven corrupteth the whole lump.
08_interl95: that no one take anything thence for himself
08_interl96: the Gentiles converted to the faith, who before played the harlot with idols
08_interl98: go "into the whole world and preach the gospel to every creature"
08_interl99: that is, bring nothing worldly with you into the Church
08_interl100: "A little leaven corrupteth the whole lump."
08_marg54: THE SAME. All the people is said to have shouted with a great shout, or, according to others, to have made jubilee with a great jubilee. Of this jubilee it is said: "Make jubilee to God, all the earth"; and elsewhere: "Blessed is the people that knoweth jubilation." He did not say "that worketh justice" or "that knoweth mysteries", but "that knoweth jubilation". In other places the fear of the Lord makes good or blessed, but only one man: "For blessed, he says, is the man that feareth the Lord." Elsewhere also many are made blessed, as the poor in spirit, or the meek, or the peacemakers, or the clean of heart. But this beatitude, poured out, makes blessed a whole people, namely, that which knoweth jubilation. Whence this jubilation seems to me to signify a certain affection of concord and unanimity; which, if it fall upon two or three disciples of Christ, whatsoever they shall ask in the name of the Saviour shall be done for them. But if the beatitude be so great that the whole people remain of one mind, say the same thing, in the same mind and the same judgment, when such a people lifts up its voice with one accord, there will happen what is written in the Acts of the Apostles: that a great earthquake was made where the apostles were praying with one mind with the women and Mary the mother of Jesus; and by this earthquake all earthly things would fall and the world itself would be overthrown. To this Jesus exhorts, saying: "Have confidence, I have overcome the world." Under his leadership, then, the world is now conquered for us, and its walls have fallen, on which the men of the world relied.
08_marg55: Let each of us fulfil these things in himself. Thou hast Jesus in thee as leader through faith. "Make thee beaten trumpets" from the holy Scriptures; draw thence thy meanings, thence thy words; for that is why they are called beaten trumpets. Sound on them, that is, in psalms, in hymns, in spiritual canticles. If thou sound on such trumpets and carry the ark of the testament round seven times, that is, if thou do not separate the mystical precepts of the law from the trumpets of the Gospel; if also thou require of thyself the consent of jubilation, that is, if the people of thy thoughts and senses always utter a concordant and harmonious voice; and if thou do not sometimes speak the truth and sometimes lie in flattering; if thou art not now soft with slackness, now savage with anger; and if within thee the flesh does not lust against the spirit and the spirit against the flesh: send forth the voice of jubilation, because the world is conquered for thee. Hence Paul said: "But God forbid that I should glory, save in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, by whom the world is crucified to me, and I to the world."
08_interl102: the worship of idols, the deceit of divination and the like
08_marg56: At the coming of Jesus the walls of Jericho were overthrown; that is, at the coming of Christ the world is conquered; whence Paul: that which was contrary to us he took out of the way, fastening it to the cross; and despoiling the principalities and powers, he hath exposed them confidently, triumphing over them on the wood of the cross. From these words I understand that the heavenly virtues, principalities and powers, seeing the battle of Jesus, the strong man bound and his goods plundered, sounded the heavenly trumpets, because, the prince of the world being bound, the world is conquered; and the heavenly host gave the voice of jubilation to the king in his triumph. Truly, then, the people of the Gentiles is set free, which knows this jubilation and acknowledges and believes the mysteries.
08_marg57: ADAMANTIUS. "Jesus saved alive Rahab the harlot and all the house of her father, and she was added to Israel unto this present day", etc. How was she added unto this present day? For this is the custom of holy Scripture, to say it of things that remain until the end of life or of the world: as "this is the father of the Moabites unto this present day", that is, until the end of the world; and "this word was spread abroad among the Jews unto this present day", that is, as long as the world stands. But how was Rahab added to the house of Israel unto this present day? Is her posterity ascribed to the mother, so that she seems to be preserved in her offspring? Or is it rather to be understood that she has truly been joined to Israel unto this present day? For the branch of the wild olive is set, that is, grafted, into the root of the good olive and joined to Israel unto this present day; because we who were taken from the Gentiles into their root, who once played the harlot, worshipping wood and stone for God, have been made above through the faith of Christ, but that people below through unbelief. For he who has in himself Christ, who is the head of all, is made the head; but those who denied him are made the tail, and those who were first are made last.
08_interl103: because the branches cut from the wild olive have been grafted into the root of the fatness of the olive
